transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
Well, I've been getting out of breath climbing the stairs. It's been bothering me and my wife's noticed it too.
Can you tell me a bit more about when you first noticed this, how it came on, and whether you have any allergies or have ever had a bad reaction to a medicine?
Just since last week, really. As for allergies, I don't have any — never had a bad reaction to any medicine.
Could you tell me how this is affecting your day-to-day life, if at all, and what medicines you're taking — including anything new or changed, and how much you take if you know?

It's mainly the stairs — I have to stop halfway up to catch my breath, and I never used to need to do that. My medicines are rivaroxaban 15 mg once a day with my evening meal, bisoprolol 5 mg once a day, atorvastatin 40 mg at night, and ramipril 2.5 mg once a day. Nothing new or changed.
Could you tell me a bit about your past health — any ongoing conditions, other illnesses, operations, or times you’ve been in hospital?

I've had an irregular heartbeat — atrial fibrillation — for about 5 years now, and I had a heart attack about 12 years ago. I also had a heart scan at the hospital last year, but I'm afraid I don't remember what they told me about it.
How much is this affecting you these days — is it stopping you from doing things you'd normally do?
It's mostly the stairs — I worry about being able to get up them to bed at night, and I'm wondering whether my heart is getting worse. Otherwise I'm not too bad.
When the breathlessness comes on going up the stairs, does anything else happen along with it?
Well, I've noticed my ankles get a bit puffy in the evening, and I use two pillows now instead of one. I don't get any chest pain, and I'm not coughing up blood or running a fever.
When you get out of breath on the stairs, where do you notice that feeling in your body, and does it move or spread anywhere else?
It's just a breathlessness all over — I feel it in my chest and I'm puffing, really. It doesn't spread to my arm or anything like that, and there's no pain with it.
Does the breathlessness come and go, or is it there most of the time?
It only comes on when I'm doing something — like going up the stairs or walking uphill. When I'm sitting or resting, I'm not breathless at all.
How would you describe the feeling of being out of breath when you climb the stairs?
It's like I can't get enough air in — I have to stop and puff for a couple of minutes before I can carry on. It eases off once I've rested, and then I'm fine again.
Is there anything else about your past health, or any operations or hospital stays, that you’d like to add?
No, I don't think so — that's about it, as far as I can recall.
Is there anything else you’ve noticed along with the breathlessness that you’d like to add?
No, I don't think there's anything else I've noticed.
How bad would you say the breathlessness is when you climb stairs — mild, moderate, or severe, or are you not sure?
I'd say it's moderate — I have to stop halfway up our stairs, and there are 14 of them. I used to manage the whole flight without stopping, so it's definitely gotten harder.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
